name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index $4,389 per 40ft on 5 Nov, down 1% on the week but above the $4,000 Alert line; next print 12 Nov
state: Drewry's World Container Index stood at $4,389 per 40ft container on 5 Nov, down 1% on the week and 124% higher than a year earlier (Drewry). That is above the $4,000 Alert line and remains the latest published reading as of 11 Nov; the next assessment is due on 12 Nov. Rates have eased slowly from a peak of $4,434 on 1 Oct, but disruption around Hormuz keeps Gulf-bound cargo exposed.
for_you: High container rates feed through to import costs for retailers and manufacturers, usually with a lag of a few months. Delivery times on Asia–Europe and Gulf routes can be longer and less predictable than usual.
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
